model_player_facing_text: Rain spatters against the soot-dark stone of Cinderwatch's eastern gate, where frayed banners flutter reluctantly in the chill wind. Refugees huddle in threadbare cloaks, while wagons and foot traffic strain the muddy approach, pressing tightly against the guards who hold the narrow choke with weary discipline. A threadbare watcher stands apart, still and watchful, eyes flicking from packs to faces in the queue. Nearby, a tavern runner calls out warmly, hawking hot stew and whispered rumors to those waiting. A well-appointed townhouse overlooking the square bears noble colors, silently contrasting the day's muddy clamor below. A large notice board lists recently imposed taxes, curfew rules, and a stark warning concerning a missing patrol, drawing uneasy glances from the crowd.

"Looks like the patrol vanished near some muddy footprints northwest of the crates," the tavern runner says, nodding toward the damp, cluttered area beyond the gate. "That's the last anyone saw of them. Beyond that, the trail grows cold."

"I'm afraid I can't say which crates those were northwest of, nor who exactly found the footprints first," the tavern runner says with a shrug, eyes flicking to the damp, cluttered area beyond the gate. "Those details haven't filtered back to me yet. As for cheap lodging and work, your best bet might be to ask around in the Market Quarter—it's a rough place, but there's usually a handful of scrappy inns and some day labor if you keep your ears open."

"Northwest of the crates is a damp, cluttered area beyond the gate where some muddy footprints were found," the tavern runner replies cautiously. "As for who first spotted them, I don't have that detail. Regarding shelter and work, I don't know where to find cheap lodging or honest employment, but you might ask around inside the town or check the notice board for postings."

"I didn't see the patrol leave, nor did I notice anyone checking those footprints," the threadbare watcher says, voice low and wary. "My eyes are often drawn elsewhere—faces and movements that slip past most—but this time, I have nothing for you on that matter." Their gaze flickers briefly toward the damp crates, then back to you, unreadable.

"My eyes tend to seek out what others overlook—those subtle shifts in the crowd," the threadbare watcher says quietly. "Today, a few faces have lingered too long near the crates, their movements a bit too deliberate. Nothing outright suspicious, but enough to warrant a closer watch. If you want to trace the missing patrol, I'd suggest checking near the northwest side past those crates; muddy footprints were noted there."

"My eyes have been caught more by the quiet watchers than the usual bustle," the threadbare watcher replies cautiously. "There are faces that linger too long, their movements too deliberate for mere travelers. But I can't say I spotted anything outright reckless or dangerous today. If you want sharper eyes, perhaps you should speak with the guard captain above—he's got a better vantage and keeps a keen watch on arrivals."

"I haven't noticed anything truly out of the ordinary today," the threadbare watcher says carefully, their gaze flickering around the gate's bustling crowd without lingering. "Eyes elsewhere, mostly on the usual faces and weary travelers passing through."

"Captain Thoran commands the gate watch tonight," one of the weary gate guards replies with a tired but steady voice. "As for hiring capable help, you'd best speak to the guard captain stationed near the roster board over there." They glance toward the serjeant managing the crowd. "He decides who gets called up for duties like searching for the missing patrol."

"Captain Thoran rubs his chin thoughtfully, eyes narrowing slightly. "I don't have any special information to share beyond what you've already heard—the patrol vanished near the muddy footprints northwest of the crates. If you're eager to help, I would need someone reliable and discreet. Reporting back regularly and keeping to assigned tasks will be essential. Beyond that, official orders will come from the serjeant managing the crowd by the roster board."

He looks to you steadily, awaiting your decision.

"Official assignments come through me, serjeant managing the crowd," the gate serjeant says with steady authority. "For aiding in the patrol search, you'll be tasked with scouting the muddy northwest track beyond the crates and reporting anything unusual you find. As for payment, compensation will be handed out once credible information is verified and relayed back here. Discretion and consistent communication are essential, but the exact sum depends on how much you contribute to locating the missing patrol."

The gate serjeant glances around the busy square before replying, "Captain Thoran has the patrol's details, but as for your assignment, you’ll be tasked with scouting the northwest trail near the crates—where the patrol was last seen. Keep a low profile, report your findings directly here at the gate, and avoid unnecessary risks. Payment will be arranged once you're officially on task; for now, prepare for the unexpected." He shifts his weight, eyes scanning the crowd for any signs of unrest.

The gate serjeant furrows their brow and shakes their head slightly. "I don’t have a headcount of the missing patrol members, nor detailed descriptions of their appearances. They were due back some hours ago from a route northwest of here, near the crates where some muddy footprints were found. Beyond that, Captain Thoran keeps stricter details reserved. If you want precise information, you’d best speak to him directly or keep watch for orders from the serjeant managing the crowd by the roster board."

"I don't have the exact count of missing patrol members, nor detailed descriptions to help you recognize them," the gate serjeant replies with a measured tone. "They were expected to return some hours ago after scouting the northwest trail past the crates, but that is all the precise information currently available. If you want more specifics, you might need to speak directly with Captain Thoran or check by the roster board for updates."
